# Tools

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:tools` from src/tools.mjs. Do not edit by hand. -->

79 tools. Every tool that changes WARUDO needs the write lease; the MCP server takes it for you when no other agent holds it.

| Kind | Meaning | Lease |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `read` | read-only | no |
| `free` | writes bridge files only | no |
| `lease` | lease control | no |
| `set` | changes WARUDO (absolute values, safe to repeat) | yes |
| `write` | changes WARUDO | yes |
| `destructive` | removes or replaces user state | yes |

## Session and lease

| Tool | Kind | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`warudo_status`](#warudo_status) | read | Bridge status |
| [`warudo_lease_status`](#warudo_lease_status) | read | Lease status |
| [`warudo_lease_acquire`](#warudo_lease_acquire) | lease | Acquire lease |
| [`warudo_lease_release`](#warudo_lease_release) | lease | Release lease |

### warudo_status

Read the live bridge heartbeat: WARUDO pid, sessionId, open scene, frame, lease owner, and runtime version. Call this first.

Kind: `read` (read-only). Runtime operation: `status`.

No parameters.

### warudo_lease_status

Read the current write lease without changing it.

Kind: `read` (read-only). Runtime operation: `lease.status`.

No parameters.

### warudo_lease_acquire

Acquire or extend the write lease for this client. The MCP server does this automatically before a write when the lease is free.

Kind: `lease` (lease control). Runtime operation: `lease.acquire`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `seconds` | number |  | (5..600, default 120) |

### warudo_lease_release

Release this client's write lease so another agent can write.

Kind: `lease` (lease control). Runtime operation: `lease.release`.

No parameters.

| Tool | Kind | Summary |

### warudo_plugin_list

List the loaded WARUDO plugins, which hold the values shown on the Settings tab: type id (e.g. "Warudo.NiloToon" = URP/NiloToon, "Warudo.Core" = render resolution, DLSS), name, version, author, entity id and field count. query filters by id, name or author.

Kind: `read` (read-only). Runtime operation: `plugin.list`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string |  |  |

### warudo_plugin_fields

Discover a plugin's Settings-tab fields (types, labels, enum choices) and triggers. Pass fields to read current values. Same shape as warudo_asset_fields.

Kind: `read` (read-only). Runtime operation: `plugin.fields`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pluginId` | string | yes | Plugin type id (e.g. "Warudo.NiloToon", "Warudo.Core") or plugin entity id, both from warudo_plugin_list. |
| `fields` | string[] |  | Field names or dotted paths to read with current values. |
| `path` | string |  | Nested structured data path to list. |
| `query` | string |  |  |
| `offset` | integer |  | (>= 0) |
| `limit` | integer |  | (1..80) |

### warudo_plugin_patch

Set Settings-tab fields of a plugin (booleans, numbers, enums, strings, vectors, colors). Validated first and rolled back on failure, like warudo_asset_patch; returns before and after. The change is applied live and saved to Plugins/Data/<id>.json the way the Settings tab saves it. Some settings change the whole renderer: Warudo.NiloToon Enabled switches the render pipeline (true = URP, false = Built-in); the reply carries renderingPipeline before/after so you can see it took effect. WARUDO reports no restart requirement for plugin settings (restartReported is always false), so verify the effect instead of assuming it, and restore the before values when you are done.

Kind: `set` (changes WARUDO (absolute values, safe to repeat)). Runtime operation: `plugin.patch`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pluginId` | string | yes | Plugin type id (e.g. "Warudo.NiloToon", "Warudo.Core") or plugin entity id, both from warudo_plugin_list. |
| `fields` | object | yes | Field name (dotted path for nested data, e.g. "LeftHandIK.Enabled") to new value. |

### warudo_character_pose_get

Read the character's current humanoid pose: all 95 Unity muscles (name, value, degree range), body height/rotation, and optional bone rotations. Use it before posing from a reference image.

Kind: `read` (read-only). Runtime operation: `character.pose.get`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `assetId` | string |  | Character asset UUID. Optional when the scene has one character or a character is selected. |
| `includeBones` | boolean |  | (default true) |
| `query` | string |  | Muscle name substring filter, e.g. "Arm" or "Left Hand". |

### warudo_character_pose_set

Pose the character. Aim bones and/or set Unity muscles (-1..1); anything not given keeps the base pose. Every joint is held inside the avatar's humanoid range (muscles -1..1), so only poses a person could take are possible; the reply lists joints that hit their limit (limited) so you can ease that aim. The pose is baked into a small .anim and played as the idle animation, so tracking and IK still layer on top. The reply comes once the character shows the pose (shown.matched; shown.furthestMuscle names what another layer still moves, shown.replacedBy an idle that took over), so a capture right after sees it. Capture with warudo_camera_capture, compare with the reference, and adjust.

Kind: `write` (changes WARUDO). Runtime operation: `character.pose.set`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `assetId` | string |  | Character asset UUID. Optional when the scene has one character or a character is selected. |
| `base` | `applied` \| `standing` \| `current` \| `neutral` |  | applied: last pose set by the bridge (else standing). standing: this avatar standing straight (from its rest skeleton), arms at the sides. current: what is on screen now. neutral: all muscles 0, which bends hips and knees. The pose covers the whole body, so aim the legs too unless standing is wanted. (default "applied") |
| `muscles` | object |  | Muscle name (see warudo_character_pose_get) or index to value, e.g. {"Left Arm Down-Up": 0.6}. |
| `bones` | object |  | HumanBodyBones name to {"aim":[x,y,z]} (point the bone toward its child; x = right, y = up, z = forward of the frame chosen by space) or {"rotate":[x,y,z]} (extra local euler degrees). Example: {"LeftUpperArm":{"aim":[-1,1,0]},"LeftLowerArm":{"aim":[0,1,0]}}. Legs too: UpperLeg, LowerLeg, Foot. Bones are posed parent first down the humanoid hierarchy (hips, spine, chest, then neck/head and arms; hips, then legs), after muscles and body values, so turning the spine or chest with muscles carries the arms and head with it. |
| `space` | `body` \| `character` |  | body: each aim is read in the frame of the torso part the bone hangs from, as currently posed (hips for spine and legs, chest for arms, neck and head). character: the character's root frame, ignoring torso turns. (default "body") |
| `bodyRotation` | [x, y, z] |  | Hips orientation, euler degrees relative to the character (0,0,0 = level, facing forward). Unset keeps the base pose hips. The hips are the root of the hierarchy: spine and chest muscles bend the body above them. |
| `hipsHeight` | number |  | Hips height above the character's floor in meters, e.g. about 0.3 to 0.4 kneeling upright or 0.15 sitting on the heels. Easier than bodyHeight; wins over it. Aims and joint limits never move the hips: they stay where the base, bodyHeight or hipsHeight put them. (0..3) |
| `bodyHeight` | number |  | Unity body height in normalized human scale (about 1 when standing). Prefer hipsHeight. (0..3) |

### warudo_character_pose_clear

| `assetId` | string |  | Character asset UUID. Optional when the scene has one character or a character is selected. |

### warudo_character_pose_save

Save a pose as a Unity humanoid .anim clip. from=applied saves the last bridge pose; from=live captures whatever the character shows now. destination=warudo saves into WARUDO's CharacterAnimations folder and returns its URI; destination=path writes to an absolute .anim path (e.g. inside a Unity project).

Kind: `write` (changes WARUDO). Runtime operation: `character.pose.save`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `assetId` | string |  | Character asset UUID. Optional when the scene has one character or a character is selected. |
| `name` | string | yes | Clip and file name without extension. |
| `from` | `applied` \| `live` |  | (default "applied") |
| `destination` | `warudo` \| `path` |  | (default "warudo") |
| `path` | string |  | Absolute .anim file path when destination=path. |
| `overwrite` | boolean |  | (default false) |

Configure one IK chain. targetPosition (world) creates or moves an anchor named "Agent IK <chain>" and targets it; targetAssetId targets an existing asset. Weights are 0..1.

| `assetId` | string |  | Character asset UUID. Optional when the scene has one character or a character is selected. |
| `chain` | `Spine` \| `LeftHand` \| `RightHand` \| `LeftFoot` \| `RightFoot` | yes |  |
| `enabled` | boolean |  |  |
| `targetAssetId` | string |  | Asset UUID to follow, or "" to clear the target. |
| `targetPosition` | [x, y, z] |  |  |
| `targetRotation` | [x, y, z] |  |  |
| `positionWeight` | number |  | (0..1) |
| `rotationWeight` | number |  | (0..1) |
| `bendGoalAssetId` | string |  | Asset UUID for the elbow/knee bend goal, or "" to clear. |
| `bendGoalWeight` | number |  | (0..1) |

### warudo_analysis_capture

Render the character (or any asset) for inspection instead of for looks: no background, no materials, several viewpoints in one image. clay = flat mannequin colored by body part (left warm, right cool; upper limb dark, lower limb light, hand/foot pale). skeleton = bones and joints by part over a faint silhouette (best for checking a pose). wireframe = visible triangle edges by part. Also draws the floor grid, the character facing (green arrow) and where the face points (magenta), and returns contacts: for each hand and foot, the distance to the nearest other body part among the drawn meshes (negative = sunk inside) and the height above the floor, plus floorClearance: the lowest mesh point of each body part (on the floor, above, or below it) for kneeling, sitting and lying poses. With the camera view it also returns joints: where every humanoid joint lands in the camera frame (0..1), to line a pose up with a reference image numerically. Nothing in WARUDO changes; use this rather than warudo_camera_capture when checking poses, contact with the floor, or mesh shape.

Kind: `read` (read-only). Runtime operation: `analysis.capture`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `assetId` | string |  | Asset UUID from warudo_asset_list or warudo_scene_get. |
| `mode` | `clay` \| `skeleton` \| `wireframe` |  | (default "clay") |
| `views` | `camera` \| `front` \| `back` \| `left` \| `right` \| `top` \| `front-left` \| `front-right` \| `back-left` \| `back-right`[] |  | Viewpoints, default camera, front, right, top. All but camera are orthographic and relative to the character (right = the character's right side). |
| `include` | string[] |  | Keep only renderers whose path contains one of these (e.g. just the body mesh to see whether a hand sinks into the chest). The reply lists renderer paths. |
| `exclude` | string[] |  | Hide renderers whose path contains any of these (e.g. hair that covers the body). |
| `bones` | boolean |  | Draw the skeleton on top (default on except wireframe). |
| `floor` | boolean |  | (default true) |
| `size` | integer |  | Pixels per view. (256..1024, default 560) |

### warudo_screen_capture

Capture the final WARUDO frame including screen-space UI and return the PNG, fitted to maxSize (default 1600, so a 2560x1440 window comes back at 1600x900; maxSize 4096 keeps full resolution). Zoom with region or around (cropped at full resolution first, so small text stays readable) and add grid to read coordinates off the image. The reply lists the crop used, the numbers of the image mapping and an imageId. The reply carries an imageId and a mapping; to click where you see something in the image you received, pass space="image" with x/y of that image to a pointer tool.

Kind: `read` (read-only). Runtime operation: `screen.capture`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `timeoutMs` | integer |  | (100..10000, default 2000) |
| `maxSize` | integer |  | Longest side of the returned PNG in pixels. The image is never enlarged. 4096 keeps a 2560x1440 window at full resolution; 1600 is about what a model is shown 1:1. (256..4096, default 1600) |
| `grid` | boolean |  | Overlay a coordinate grid (thin two-tone lines at about 25 % opacity) labeled in WINDOW pixels at the top and left edges, however the image is cropped or scaled, so click coordinates can be read straight off the image. (default false) |
| `gridStep` | integer |  | Window pixels between grid lines. Passing it turns the grid on. (10..1000, default 100) |
| `region` | number[] |  | [x, y, width, height] in window pixels (top-left origin), cropped at full resolution before the image is fitted to maxSize. Must lie inside the window. |
| `around` | object |  | Frame an object instead of a region: { objectId } or { path } of a UI object (its RectTransform on screen, plugin overlay panels included) or of a renderer or GameObject (its bounds projected with the main camera). The reply returns the crop used. |
| `padding` | integer |  | Window pixels added around the framed object. (0..400, default 16) |
| `space` | `pixels` \| `image` |  | pixels: window pixels. image: pixels of an image a capture tool returned (the latest one, or the one named by imageId), so a point read off that image is clicked exactly there with no scale math. Applies to region and points. (default "pixels") |
| `imageId` | string |  | With space=image: the imageId from the capture reply. Default: the latest image of this MCP server (it keeps the last 32). |

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `assetId` | string |  | Asset UUID from warudo_asset_list or warudo_scene_get. |
| `x` | number | yes | (0..1) |
| `y` | number | yes | (0..1) |
| `select` | boolean |  | (default true) |

### warudo_pointer_click

Click (or double click) at a point of the WARUDO main window with a virtual mouse, without bringing WARUDO to the front. The click is played into WARUDO's UI for a few frames through Unity's input module; no OS input is sent. It reaches the main-window UI and plugins that read the virtual pointer; it does not move the WARUDO camera, reach the WARUDO editor window, or reach code that reads Input.* directly. x/y (and path) are in the image you received when you pass space="image": pixels of the latest capture image, or of the one named by imageId. Find the point with warudo_ui_list or warudo_ui_at, or use warudo_ui_click for a control you know by its label. The reply says what was under the pointer at press and release and which object received the click. A double click needs about 15 frames per second or more to count as one.

Kind: `write` (changes WARUDO). Runtime operation: `pointer.play, with a frame timeline the MCP server builds from the arguments`. Needs runtime feature `pointer`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | number | yes | Horizontal position, left to right. |
| `y` | number | yes | Vertical position, top to bottom. |
| `space` | `pixels` \| `normalized` \| `image` |  | pixels: window pixels, origin top-left (what warudo_ui_list returns). normalized: 0..1 of the window. image: pixels of an image a capture tool returned (the latest one, or the one named by imageId), so a point read off that image is clicked exactly there with no scale math. (default "pixels") |
| `imageId` | string |  | With space=image: the imageId from the capture reply. Default: the latest image of this MCP server (it keeps the last 32). |
| `button` | `left` \| `right` \| `middle` |  | (default "left") |
| `count` | `1` \| `2` |  | (default 1) |
| `modifiers` | `ctrl` \| `shift` \| `alt`[] |  | Virtual modifier keys held for the whole gesture. Code that reads the virtual keys (see the README) sees them; WARUDO hotkeys do not. |
| `holdFrames` | integer |  | Frames the button stays down (at most 4 for a double click). (1..30, default 2) |
| `settleFrames` | integer |  | Frames to wait after the gesture, with the pointer still in place, so the UI has reacted before the reply (and the capture). (0..60, default 2) |
| `expectObject` | integer |  | Instance id of the UI object that must be under the pointer (or inside it) when the button goes down, from warudo_ui_list. If something else is on top the gesture stops before pressing with COVERED. |
| `capture` | boolean |  | Also capture the screen after settleFrames, with the virtual pointer still in place (hover and pressed looks included), and return it as an image (it carries an imageId like any capture). maxSize, grid, gridStep, region, around and padding shape that image and need capture=true. (default false) |
| `maxSize` | integer |  | Longest side of the returned PNG in pixels. The image is never enlarged. 4096 keeps a 2560x1440 window at full resolution; 1600 is about what a model is shown 1:1. (256..4096, default 1600) |
| `grid` | boolean |  | Overlay a coordinate grid (thin two-tone lines at about 25 % opacity) labeled in WINDOW pixels at the top and left edges, however the image is cropped or scaled, so click coordinates can be read straight off the image. (default false) |
| `gridStep` | integer |  | Window pixels between grid lines. Passing it turns the grid on. (10..1000, default 100) |
| `region` | number[] |  | [x, y, width, height] in window pixels (top-left origin), cropped at full resolution before the image is fitted to maxSize. Must lie inside the window. |
| `around` | object |  | Frame an object instead of a region: { objectId } or { path } of a UI object (its RectTransform on screen, plugin overlay panels included) or of a renderer or GameObject (its bounds projected with the main camera). The reply returns the crop used. |
| `padding` | integer |  | Window pixels added around the framed object. (0..400, default 16) |

### warudo_pointer_drag

Press at the first point, move along the path one small step per frame, and release on the last point, with the virtual mouse. For sliders, scroll bars, sorting and window resizing. Give frames per segment or totalFrames for the whole path. It reaches the main-window UI and plugins that read the virtual pointer; it does not move the WARUDO camera, reach the WARUDO editor window, or reach code that reads Input.* directly. x/y (and path) are in the image you received when you pass space="image": pixels of the latest capture image, or of the one named by imageId. The gesture is limited to 600 frames and 64 points.

(default "pixels") |

(default false) |
| `maxSize` | integer |  | Longest side of the returned PNG in pixels. The image is never enlarged. 4096 keeps a 2560x1440 window at full resolution; 1600 is about what a model is shown 1:1. (256..4096, default 1600) |

| `padding` | integer |  | Window pixels added around the framed object. (0..400, default 16) |

### warudo_pointer_move

It reaches the main-window UI and plugins that read the virtual pointer; it does not move the WARUDO camera, reach the WARUDO editor window, or reach code that reads Input.* directly. x/y (and path) are in the image you received when you pass space="image": pixels of the latest capture image, or of the one named by imageId.

### warudo_pointer_button

Press (down) or release (up) one mouse button, optionally at x and y first, for gestures made of several calls: button down, a few warudo_pointer_move calls with keep, button up. A button left down keeps the virtual pointer parked until the matching up, a warudo_pointer_release, the lease ending, or pointer.idleReleaseMs of no use. Modifiers are held only during this call. It reaches the main-window UI and plugins that read the virtual pointer; it does not move the WARUDO camera, reach the WARUDO editor window, or reach code that reads Input.* directly. x/y (and path) are in the image you received when you pass space="image": pixels of the latest capture image, or of the one named by imageId.

Kind: `write` (changes WARUDO). Runtime operation: `pointer.play, with a frame timeline the MCP server builds from the arguments`. Needs runtime feature `pointer`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | `down` \| `up` | yes |  |
| `button` | `left` \| `right` \| `middle` |  | (default "left") |
| `x` | number |  | Horizontal position, left to right. |
| `y` | number |  | Vertical position, top to bottom. |
| `space` | `pixels` \| `normalized` \| `image` |  | pixels: window pixels, origin top-left (what warudo_ui_list returns). normalized: 0..1 of the window. image: pixels of an image a capture tool returned (the latest one, or the one named by imageId), so a point read off that image is clicked exactly there with no scale math. (default "pixels") |
| `imageId` | string |  | With space=image: the imageId from the capture reply. Default: the latest image of this MCP server (it keeps the last 32). |
| `modifiers` | `ctrl` \| `shift` \| `alt`[] |  | Virtual modifier keys held for the whole gesture. Code that reads the virtual keys (see the README) sees them; WARUDO hotkeys do not. |
| `settleFrames` | integer |  | Frames to wait after the gesture, with the pointer still in place, so the UI has reacted before the reply (and the capture). (0..60, default 2) |
| `expectObject` | integer |  | Instance id of the UI object that must be under the pointer (or inside it) when the button goes down, from warudo_ui_list. If something else is on top the gesture stops before pressing with COVERED. |
| `capture` | boolean |  | Also capture the screen after settleFrames, with the virtual pointer still in place (hover and pressed looks included), and return it as an image (it carries an imageId like any capture). maxSize, grid, gridStep, region, around and padding shape that image and need capture=true. (default false) |
| `maxSize` | integer |  | Longest side of the returned PNG in pixels. The image is never enlarged. 4096 keeps a 2560x1440 window at full resolution; 1600 is about what a model is shown 1:1. (256..4096, default 1600) |
| `grid` | boolean |  | Overlay a coordinate grid (thin two-tone lines at about 25 % opacity) labeled in WINDOW pixels at the top and left edges, however the image is cropped or scaled, so click coordinates can be read straight off the image. (default false) |
| `gridStep` | integer |  | Window pixels between grid lines. Passing it turns the grid on. (10..1000, default 100) |
| `region` | number[] |  | [x, y, width, height] in window pixels (top-left origin), cropped at full resolution before the image is fitted to maxSize. Must lie inside the window. |
| `around` | object |  | Frame an object instead of a region: { objectId } or { path } of a UI object (its RectTransform on screen, plugin overlay panels included) or of a renderer or GameObject (its bounds projected with the main camera). The reply returns the crop used. |
| `padding` | integer |  | Window pixels added around the framed object. (0..400, default 16) |

It reaches the main-window UI and plugins that read the virtual pointer; it does not move the WARUDO camera, reach the WARUDO editor window, or reach code that reads Input.* directly. x/y (and path) are in the image you received when you pass space="image": pixels of the latest capture image, or of the one named by imageId.

### warudo_pointer_release

End any virtual pointer, button or key state and give WARUDO its real mouse input and window focus back. Held buttons and keys are let go first. Safe to call at any time; does nothing when no virtual pointer is active.

Kind: `set` (changes WARUDO (absolute values, safe to repeat)). Runtime operation: `pointer.release`. Needs runtime feature `pointer`.

No parameters.

### warudo_pointer_state

Read the virtual pointer: whether it is active, which input module and EventSystem it feeds, held buttons and keys, its position, the window size, what is under it, the selected UI object, and whether the feature is enabled (config.json pointer.enabled).

Kind: `read` (read-only). Runtime operation: `pointer.state`. Needs runtime feature `pointer`.

No parameters.

### warudo_key_virtual

Hold, press or release a virtual keyboard key (a Unity KeyCode name such as Space, A, LeftShift, Return). Only code that reads the virtual keys sees it (the plugin contract in the README); WARUDO hotkeys and blueprints use warudo_input_key instead. A key left down stays down until released, the lease ends, or pointer.idleReleaseMs of no use.

Kind: `write` (changes WARUDO). Runtime operation: `pointer.play, with a frame timeline the MCP server builds from the arguments`. Needs runtime feature `pointer`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | string | yes | Unity KeyCode name. |
| `action` | `press` \| `down` \| `up` |  | (default "press") |
| `frames` | integer |  | Frames a press holds the key. (1..60, default 2) |

### warudo_ui_list

List the active, visible controls of the WARUDO main window that react to the pointer (buttons, sliders, toggles, scroll areas and anything with a click, press, drag or scroll handler), frontmost canvas first. Each has an id, path, handler types, label (first text in it), rectangle [x, y, width, height] and center in window pixels, its kind (button, toggle, slider, input, scroll or other), whether it is interactable and on screen, and hidden=true when its canvas object carries HideFlags (a plugin overlay such as a Color Studio panel). region keeps the controls that overlap a window rectangle. Use the center with warudo_pointer_click, or warudo_ui_click to click one by label.

Kind: `read` (read-only). Runtime operation: `ui.list`. Needs runtime feature `pointer`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string |  | Substring of the label or path, case-insensitive. |
| `id` | integer |  | Only the element with this id. |
| `region` | number[] |  | [x, y, width, height] in window pixels: only controls whose rectangle overlaps it. With space=image, in pixels of an image you received. |
| `space` | `pixels` \| `image` |  | pixels: window pixels. image: pixels of an image a capture tool returned (the latest one, or the one named by imageId), so a point read off that image is clicked exactly there with no scale math. Applies to region and points. (default "pixels") |
| `imageId` | string |  | With space=image: the imageId from the capture reply. Default: the latest image of this MCP server (it keeps the last 32). |
| `interactableOnly` | boolean |  | Hide controls that are disabled or blocked by a canvas group. (default true) |
| `offset` | integer |  | (>= 0) |
| `limit` | integer |  | (1..500) |

### warudo_ui_at

Read what is under a point of the WARUDO main window: every UI raycast hit front to back (path, module, depth, sorting order, distance), whether the pointer is over UI at all, and the objects that would receive a click, a drag and a wheel turn there. Use it to see what covers a control. Pass space="image" to give x/y in pixels of an image you received.

Kind: `read` (read-only). Runtime operation: `ui.at`. Needs runtime feature `pointer`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | number | yes | Horizontal position, left to right. |
| `y` | number | yes | Vertical position, top to bottom. |
| `space` | `pixels` \| `normalized` \| `image` |  | pixels: window pixels, origin top-left (what warudo_ui_list returns). normalized: 0..1 of the window. image: pixels of an image a capture tool returned (the latest one, or the one named by imageId), so a point read off that image is clicked exactly there with no scale math. (default "pixels") |
| `imageId` | string |  | With space=image: the imageId from the capture reply. Default: the latest image of this MCP server (it keeps the last 32). |

### warudo_ui_click

Click a control of the WARUDO main window with the virtual mouse, at the center of its rectangle. Name it by near (the visible text, exact match first, then contains; the preferred way, it also finds plugin overlay panels such as Color Studio), by mark (the number printed on the latest warudo_ui_capture image, refused with MARK_STALE when the controls on screen changed since), by label (contains, or labelMatch) or by id from warudo_ui_list. If another object covers the control the click is not sent and the reply is COVERED, so it never clicks whatever is on top. An ambiguous text needs index. capture=true returns the image with the pointer marked. It reaches the main-window UI and plugins that read the virtual pointer; it does not move the WARUDO camera, reach the WARUDO editor window, or reach code that reads Input.* directly.

Kind: `write` (changes WARUDO). Runtime operation: `pointer.play, after the MCP server finds the element with ui.list`. Needs runtime feature `pointer`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `near` | string |  | Visible text of the control: exact match first, then contains (case-insensitive). Pass one of near, mark, label or id. |
| `mark` | integer |  | Number from the latest warudo_ui_capture of this MCP server. (>= 1) |
| `id` | integer |  | Element id from warudo_ui_list. |
| `label` | string |  | Text of the control, matched by labelMatch (default contains). |
| `labelMatch` | `exact` \| `contains` \| `auto` |  | How near/label match: auto = exact first, then contains (the default for near); contains is the default for label. |
| `index` | integer |  | Which usable match to click when several match (0-based, ui.list order). (>= 0) |
| `button` | `left` \| `right` \| `middle` |  | (default "left") |
| `count` | `1` \| `2` |  | (default 1) |
| `modifiers` | `ctrl` \| `shift` \| `alt`[] |  | Virtual modifier keys held for the whole gesture. Code that reads the virtual keys (see the README) sees them; WARUDO hotkeys do not. |
| `holdFrames` | integer |  | (1..30, default 2) |
| `settleFrames` | integer |  | Frames to wait after the gesture, with the pointer still in place, so the UI has reacted before the reply (and the capture). (0..60, default 2) |
| `capture` | boolean |  | Also capture the screen after settleFrames, with the virtual pointer still in place (hover and pressed looks included), and return it as an image (it carries an imageId like any capture). maxSize, grid, gridStep, region, around and padding shape that image and need capture=true. (default false) |
| `maxSize` | integer |  | Longest side of the returned PNG in pixels. The image is never enlarged. 4096 keeps a 2560x1440 window at full resolution; 1600 is about what a model is shown 1:1. (256..4096, default 1600) |
| `grid` | boolean |  | Overlay a coordinate grid (thin two-tone lines at about 25 % opacity) labeled in WINDOW pixels at the top and left edges, however the image is cropped or scaled, so click coordinates can be read straight off the image. (default false) |
| `gridStep` | integer |  | Window pixels between grid lines. Passing it turns the grid on. (10..1000, default 100) |
| `region` | number[] |  | [x, y, width, height] in window pixels (top-left origin), cropped at full resolution before the image is fitted to maxSize. Must lie inside the window. |
| `around` | object |  | Frame an object instead of a region: { objectId } or { path } of a UI object (its RectTransform on screen, plugin overlay panels included) or of a renderer or GameObject (its bounds projected with the main camera). The reply returns the crop used. |
| `padding` | integer |  | Window pixels added around the framed object. (0..400, default 16) |

### warudo_ui_capture

Screenshot of the WARUDO window (or a region/around of it) with a numbered box over every control warudo_ui_list returns for that area, colored by kind: button orange, toggle cyan, slider magenta, input green, scroll violet, other light grey. The reply lists the legend: number, id, kind, label, path, rectangle and center in window pixels. Click one with warudo_ui_click mark=N, or read its rectangle and use warudo_pointer_drag for a slider. Same filters as warudo_ui_list (query, interactableOnly), at most limit controls (default 60, numbered in ui.list order). Plugin overlay canvases are included. Like every image tool it returns an imageId and the mapping. The reply carries an imageId and a mapping; to click where you see something in the image you received, pass space="image" with x/y of that image to a pointer tool.

Kind: `read` (read-only). Runtime operation: `ui.capture`. Needs runtime feature `capture-tools`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string |  | Substring of the label or path, case-insensitive. |
| `interactableOnly` | boolean |  | Hide controls that are disabled or blocked by a canvas group. (default true) |
| `limit` | integer |  | Most controls to box and number. (1..200, default 60) |
| `timeoutMs` | integer |  | (100..10000, default 2000) |
| `maxSize` | integer |  | Longest side of the returned PNG in pixels. The image is never enlarged. 4096 keeps a 2560x1440 window at full resolution; 1600 is about what a model is shown 1:1. (256..4096, default 1600) |
| `grid` | boolean |  | Overlay a coordinate grid (thin two-tone lines at about 25 % opacity) labeled in WINDOW pixels at the top and left edges, however the image is cropped or scaled, so click coordinates can be read straight off the image. (default false) |
| `gridStep` | integer |  | Window pixels between grid lines. Passing it turns the grid on. (10..1000, default 100) |
| `region` | number[] |  | [x, y, width, height] in window pixels (top-left origin), cropped at full resolution before the image is fitted to maxSize. Must lie inside the window. |
| `around` | object |  | Frame an object instead of a region: { objectId } or { path } of a UI object (its RectTransform on screen, plugin overlay panels included) or of a renderer or GameObject (its bounds projected with the main camera). The reply returns the crop used. |
| `padding` | integer |  | Window pixels added around the framed object. (0..400, default 16) |
| `space` | `pixels` \| `image` |  | pixels: window pixels. image: pixels of an image a capture tool returned (the latest one, or the one named by imageId), so a point read off that image is clicked exactly there with no scale math. Applies to region and points. (default "pixels") |
| `imageId` | string |  | With space=image: the imageId from the capture reply. Default: the latest image of this MCP server (it keeps the last 32). |

### warudo_ui_set_text

Put text into an input field of the WARUDO main window (UnityEngine.UI.InputField or TMP_InputField) by id from warudo_ui_list: sets the text (raising onValueChanged), then raises onEndEdit, and onSubmit when submit=true. Typing keys cannot be sent, because Unity reads typed text from the OS; this is the way to fill a field. Read-only, disabled and not-a-field targets are refused.

Kind: `write` (changes WARUDO). Runtime operation: `ui.set_text`. Needs runtime feature `pointer`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | integer | yes | Input field id from warudo_ui_list. |
| `text` | string | yes |  |
| `submit` | boolean |  | (default false) |

## Input, logs, maintenance

| Tool | Kind | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`warudo_input_key`](#warudo_input_key) | write | Send hotkey event |
| [`warudo_runtime_logs`](#warudo_runtime_logs) | read | Runtime logs |

### warudo_input_key

Broadcast a WARUDO keystroke event to blueprints. Only allowed while WARUDO has focus (hostFocused=true confirms the caller checked); never sends an OS key.

Kind: `write` (changes WARUDO). Runtime operation: `input.key`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | string | yes |  |
| `ctrl` | boolean |  |  |
| `shift` | boolean |  |  |
| `alt` | boolean |  |  |
| `meta` | boolean |  |  |
| `hostFocused` | boolean | yes |  |

### warudo_runtime_logs

Read WARUDO log lines after a sequence cursor. Secrets are redacted.

Kind: `read` (read-only). Runtime operation: `runtime.logs`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `after` | integer |  | (>= 0) |
| `limit` | integer |  | (1..500) |

### warudo_maintenance_cleanup

Delete old bridge files (responses, captures, snapshots, unused pose previews) past the retention in config.json. dryRun=true only reports, with the file names it would delete. Pose previews a character or saved scene still uses are never deleted.

Kind: `free` (writes bridge files only). Runtime operation: `maintenance.cleanup`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dryRun` | boolean |  | (default true) |
